h1:
Where to Stay in Chiang Rai?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Chiang Rai hotels across every budget — from an all-inclusive resort on the Mekong at the Golden Triangle and bamboo cottages in the Mae Salong hills down to city dorms from ฿250/night. Covering the main areas: the Golden Triangle and Chiang Saen, the Kok riverside, Mae Salong, and the city centre. From roughly ฿250–35,000/night.
heroStats: 🏞️ 4 key areas (Golden Triangle·Kok riverside·Mae Salong·City Centre)
introH2: 🏞️ Why does choosing the right area in Chiang Rai matter?
introHtml: Chiang Rai covers more ground than most people expect, and each area has a completely different feel. The Golden Triangle and Chiang Saen sit at the far north on the Mekong, about a 1.5-hour drive from the city — resort country with river views and elephant camps. The Kok riverside cuts through the city and is a calm zone of resorts and boutiques that’s still close to town. Mae Salong (Mae Chan district) is the mountain zone, with cool air and a sea-of-mist view. And the city centre around the clock tower, night bazaar and walking street is easiest for strolling and eating, with stays at every level. Many people book without checking the area, then lose hours commuting back and forth. This guide rounds up 12 Chiang Rai hotels we’ve already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Chiang Rai has no metro; you get around by rental car, motorbike, taxi, songthaew or Grab (limited). From Mae Fah Luang Airport (CEI) it’s about 15 minutes into town. Downtown around the clock tower and night bazaar is walkable, but Wat Rong Khun (the White Temple), Wat Rong Suea Ten and the Golden Triangle all need a car. The Golden Triangle and Chiang Saen are about 1.5 hours from the city. The road up to Mae Salong is winding — drive in daylight in a sound vehicle. The areas in this guide: Golden Triangle–Chiang Saen — Mekong-view resorts and elephant camps, quiet · Kok riverside — riverside resorts and boutiques, calm but close to town · Mae Salong — mountain resorts, cool air, sea-of-mist views · City Centre — clock tower, night bazaar, walking street, easy to explore.

toc.name: Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort
The Legend Chiang Rai Boutique River Resort & Spa

entries.name: Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Golden Triangle, Chiang Saen · on the Mekong
entries.storyHtml: The top score in this guide at 9.6 — Anantara Golden Triangle is an all-inclusive 5-star resort on the Mekong at the Golden Triangle, Chiang Saen. Its signature, found nowhere else here, is the in-house elephant camp with up-close elephant activities, plus the Jungle Bubble glass-dome rooms where you sleep watching elephants and stars in the forest. The rate covers meals, drinks and most activities. Real guest reviews praise the three-country Mekong view and attentive service, but flag the high price and the roughly 1.5-hour drive from Chiang Rai city.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The rate is all-inclusive, so per night it works out better value than it first looks. Jungle Bubbles are limited and sell out fast — book well ahead if you want one.
pros: Top score in this guide 9.6 — Anantara-level service
In-house elephant camp and up-close activities found nowhere else
Jungle Bubble glass domes — sleep among elephants and stars
Rate includes meals, drinks and most activities
cons: Highest price in the guide — best for a special celebration or honeymoon
In Chiang Saen, about 1.5 hours from Chiang Rai city

entries.name: The Riverie by Katathani
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kok riverside, central · walk to night bazaar
entries.storyHtml: The Riverie is a 5-star luxury resort on the Kok River in the city centre with the most reviews of any luxury pick here — 945 reviews, scoring 9.4. Its strength is a riverside location that stays quiet yet is still a walk from the night bazaar, plus a large pool overlooking the river. The surprise is that base rooms start at just ฿2,600, strong value for a 5-star resort of this level. Real guest reviews praise the value and location, though some note parts of the building are starting to show their age.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The base Deluxe is already good value; step up to Deluxe River for a direct Kok-river view from the balcony. Travelling as a family? The Family Suite works out cheaper per head.
pros: Most reviews among luxury picks, 945 · 9.4 score is reliable
Kok riverside, central — quiet yet a walk to the night bazaar
Large river-view pool, full resort feel
5-star luxury from just ฿2,600 — strong value at this level
cons: An older resort — parts of the building are showing their age
River-view rooms fill fast; book ahead if you want one

entries.name: Le Meridien Chiang Rai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kok riverside, near town · 53 sqm rooms
entries.addr: 221/2 Moo 20, Kwaewai Road, Robwieng, Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: Le Meridien is a Marriott-group 5-star boutique resort on the Kok River, near the city, scoring 9.3 from 494 reviews. Its draw is base rooms a full 53 square metres, and a riverside spot that stays peaceful yet is only a few minutes’ drive into town. Real guest reviews praise the spacious rooms, the leafy riverside gardens and Marriott-standard service. Best for travellers who want a luxury riverside resort that’s still handy for the city.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The base Deluxe is already 53 sqm; only step up to River View if you want the Kok-river view from your balcony. Marriott Bonvoy members can earn or redeem points here.
pros: Marriott group, steady service · 9.3 score
Base rooms a full 53 sqm — bigger than many rivals
Kok riverside — quiet yet minutes’ drive from town
Leafy riverside gardens and pool, made for relaxing
cons: Riverside location — not walkable to the night bazaar, you need a car
Pricier than the other entry-level riverside resorts here

entries.name: The Legend Chiang Rai Boutique River Resort & Spa
entries.addr: 124/15 Moo 21 Kohloy Road, Rim Kok, Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: The Legend is a 4-star boutique resort on the Kok River with the most reviews of any boutique pick here — over 1,442 reviews, scoring 9.2. The signature is its distinctive Lanna architecture, roomy studios with large walk-in showers, and pool villas for those who want more privacy. The Kok-riverside setting is calm and quiet. Real guest reviews praise the beautiful design and the peace, but note you need a car as it’s not walkable to town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The base Superior Studio is already spacious and good-looking; only move up to the One Bedroom Pool Villa if you’re a couple or small family wanting a private pool.
pros: Most reviews among boutique picks, 1,442 · reliable 9.2 score
Distinctive, beautifully styled Lanna architecture
Roomy studios with big walk-in showers
Quiet Kok-riverside setting, pool villas available
cons: Riverside location — not walkable to town, you need a car
A long-running resort; some corners are showing their age

entries.name: Nak Nakara Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 City centre · by the Hilltribe Museum
entries.storyHtml: Nak Nakara is a central 4-star boutique hotel decked out in Lanna style from just ฿1,500, scoring 9.3. Its strengths are a downtown location next to the Hilltribe Museum, within walking distance of the clock tower and walking street, plus a pool — rare at this price in the city centre. Real guest reviews praise the pretty Lanna decor and the easy-to-explore location. Review count is still modest (116) but the score stays consistently high.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The base Boutique Double is good value if you’re mainly here for location. Travelling as a family? Book the Family Room for 3–4 people to bring the per-head cost down.
pros: Distinctive, pretty Lanna decor · 9.3 score
Central — walk to the clock tower and walking street
Has a pool — rare at this price downtown
4-star boutique from just ฿1,500 — great value
cons: Still few reviews (116) compared with others here
Central spot — some rooms catch street noise; ask for an inner room

entries.name: Mercy Hostel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central, near clock tower · small pool
entries.storyHtml: Mercy Hostel is the most-reviewed property in this guide — over 2,970 reviews, scoring a high 9.2, with dorms from just ฿250. What sets it apart from a typical hostel: a small pool, a gym and a shared kitchen, all at dorm prices. It’s central, near the clock tower and walking street. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness, the above-price facilities and the friendly vibe. Best for backpackers and budget travellers who want more than a plain dorm.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Want quiet and privacy? Book a Studio — still cheaper than a hotel. Use the pool and the shared kitchen to save on food over a longer stay.
pros: Most-reviewed in the guide, 2,970 · high 9.2 score
Small pool, gym and shared kitchen — above its dorm price
Dorms from just ฿250, right in the city centre
Clean, friendly vibe, near the clock tower and walking street
cons: It’s a hostel — dorms mean sharing space with others
Private Studios are limited and fill fast

entries.name: Phu Chaisai Mountain Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Salong hills, Mae Chan · bamboo mountain cottages
tags: ⛰️ Bamboo cottages in the Mae Salong hills
🌄 Mountain views and sea of mist
entries.addr: 388 Moo 4, Mae Salong Nai, Mae Chan, Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: Phu Chaisai is a boutique mountain resort of bamboo cottages set high in the Mae Salong hills — an experience you won’t find in the city, scoring 8.8 from 434 reviews. Its draw is the natural mountain setting: cool air, mountain views and a morning sea of mist, bamboo cottages that put you genuinely close to nature, and mountain-view pool villas for more privacy. Real guest reviews praise the views and the calm, but flag the winding mountain road, the fair distance from town and the airport, and the open, close-to-nature bamboo cottages (the odd insect comes with the territory). Best for nature lovers wanting to escape the city.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The mountain road is winding — if self-driving, go in daylight in a sound vehicle. Wake early for the sea of mist and cool air, the highlight here. The bamboo cottages are open to nature, so pack insect repellent and a warm layer in winter.
pros: Bamboo-cottage mountain stay you won’t find elsewhere in Chiang Rai
Mountain views and a morning sea of mist, cool air
Quiet, natural setting — perfect for escaping the city
Mountain-view pool villas for more privacy
cons: Winding mountain road; a fair way from town and the airport
Open bamboo cottages close to nature — expect the odd insect

entries.name: Wiang Inn Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 City centre · near the night bazaar
entries.storyHtml: Wiang Inn is a central 4-star hotel in a prime spot right by the night bazaar, scoring 8.8 from 371 reviews. A long-established Chiang Rai hotel, it has a pool and full facilities from just ฿1,400, within walking distance of the night bazaar, markets and restaurants. Real guest reviews praise the location and value, but note the building and some rooms are showing their age — choose a renovated Deluxe.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Deluxe rooms are larger and feel newer than the base Superior. With the night bazaar next door, evening strolls and street food are easy.
pros: Central, right by the night bazaar — walk to food and sights
Has a pool and full facilities
4-star from just ฿1,400 — good value
Great for travellers who prioritise a central location
cons: A long-established hotel — building and some rooms feel dated
Ask for a renovated Deluxe; it’s newer than the Superior

entries.name: Diamond Park Inn Chiangrai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near the clock tower · city centre
entries.storyHtml: Diamond Park Inn is a central 3-star city resort near the clock tower with a pool, from just ฿1,100, scoring 8.7 from 112 reviews. Its strengths are a downtown location near the clock tower and main sights, plus a pool and parking. Real guest reviews praise the value, the clean rooms and the location, but note the facilities are basic, in line with a 3-star. Best for road-trippers who want a pool and easy parking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Good for a Chiang Rai road trip thanks to parking and the clock-tower location. The Deluxe is a touch roomier with a garden/pool view over the base Superior.
pros: Central, near the clock tower and main sights
Pool and parking, from just ฿1,100
Clean rooms, 8.7 score — good value for a central 3-star
Great for road-trippers wanting easy parking
cons: Basic facilities, in line with a 3-star
Still few reviews (112) compared with others here

entries.name: Pimanninn
entries.badge: 💬 Huge review count, has a pool
entries.storyHtml: Pimanninn is a central budget hotel with the most reviews in this guide — over 6,142, from just ฿750. It bills itself as a “Luxury Economy Hotel,” meaning a pool and gym at a budget price. The 7.9 score isn’t as high as the table-toppers, partly because the sheer review volume surfaces both praise and complaints. Real guest reviews like the value and the pool, but note the rooms and service are basic — don’t expect a big-hotel feel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Good if you want a low price but still a pool. Pay a few hundred baht more for the Deluxe or Suite to get a larger, newer room than the base Standard.
pros: Most reviews in the guide, 6,142 — plenty of data
Pool and gym from just ฿750
Central location, easy onward travel
Good for budget travellers who still want a pool
cons: 7.9 score trails the table-toppers — basic rooms and service
High review volume shows both praise and gripes; set expectations

entries.name: Baan Bua Guest House
entries.badge: 🪙 Quiet guesthouse, near the bus station
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Jetyod old-town area · near the bus station
entries.storyHtml: Baan Bua is a budget guesthouse in the Jetyod old-town area, with rooms from just ฿400, scoring 8.3 from 258 reviews. Its strengths are a quiet garden setting, a homely and friendly feel, and a spot near the bus station for easy onward travel. There are fan rooms, A/C rooms and a family room. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness, the welcoming owner and the value. Best for backpackers and budget travellers who’d rather have a quiet private room than a dorm.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: On the tightest budget, take a fan room; pay a little more for A/C in the hot season. It’s near the bus station, handy if you’re arriving or leaving by coach.
pros: Rooms from just ฿400 — good value for a private room in town
Quiet garden setting, homely and friendly
Near the bus station, easy arrivals and departures
Welcoming owner, clean rooms, 8.3 score
cons: It’s a guesthouse — basic facilities
The cheapest fan rooms can be hot in the hot season

entries.name: Phowadol Resort & Spa
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near the airport and walking street · garden cottages
entries.storyHtml: Phowadol is a 3-star garden-cottage resort near the airport and the walking street, from just ฿900, scoring 6.9 from 43 reviews — the lowest in this guide. Its draw is the leafy garden-cottage setting and a location near the airport, handy for early flights or late arrivals. Real guest reviews like the greenery and the price, but many flag that some rooms and facilities are dated and due a refresh, hence its place at the end. Best for those who weigh an airport-close location and price over newness.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Superior or Deluxe Cottage in the garden over the block Superior — they’re roomier. Good as a last-night stay before an early flight, given how close the airport is.
pros: Leafy garden cottages from just ฿900
Near the airport — handy for early flights or late arrivals
Near the walking street for evening food and strolls
Good for those prioritising an airport-close, budget stay
cons: Lowest score here, 6.9 — some rooms are dated and due a refresh
Some facilities feel aged; ask to see a renovated room

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Chiang Rai hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should tourists stay in for Chiang Rai?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style. The city centre around the clock tower and night bazaar is easiest for walking and eating, with stays at every level (Nak Nakara, Wiang Inn, Diamond Park Inn, Mercy Hostel, Pimanninn). The Kok riverside is a calm resort zone that’s still close to town (The Riverie, Le Meridien, The Legend). Mae Salong is the cool mountain zone (Phu Chaisai). And the Golden Triangle–Chiang Saen at the far north on the Mekong suits a special trip (Anantara Golden Triangle).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chiang Rai hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: dorms and guesthouses from about ฿250–650 a night; mid-range hotels and resorts up to 4-star around ฿900–3,500; 5-star luxury resorts on the Kok from about ฿2,600–9,500; and the all-inclusive resort at the Golden Triangle from about ฿35,000 (meals and activities included). All figures are approximate from-rates for standard rooms.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to visit the Golden Triangle?
faq.a: The Golden Triangle and Chiang Saen are about a 1.5-hour drive from Chiang Rai city. If you want to stay right on the Mekong and focus on the up-close elephant experience, Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort is the main choice. But if you’re using Chiang Rai as a base and visiting the Golden Triangle as a day trip, staying in the city or on the Kok riverside is more convenient and cheaper — then drive or join a tour out and back in a day.

faq.q: ❓ Is there anywhere to stay in the cool mountains in Chiang Rai?
faq.a: If you want to escape the city for cool air and a sea-of-mist view, Phu Chaisai Mountain Resort is a boutique resort of bamboo cottages in the Mae Salong hills (Mae Chan district), scoring 8.8 from 434 reviews — an experience you won’t find in the city. The mountain road is winding, so drive in daylight in a sound vehicle, and it’s a fair way from town and the airport — best for nature lovers planning a dedicated mountain night.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Chiang Rai hotel?
faq.a: On weekdays outside the tourist season, 2–4 weeks ahead is enough. But in the cool-season high season (November–February), the comfortable weather makes it popular, and around New Year and the flower festival the good rooms go very fast — book 1–2 months or more ahead.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get around Chiang Rai — do I need to rent a car?
faq.a: Chiang Rai has no metro; you mainly get around by rental car, motorbike, taxi and songthaew, plus Grab (limited). Downtown around the clock tower and night bazaar is walkable, but the White Temple, Wat Rong Suea Ten, the Golden Triangle and Mae Salong are all outside town and need a car or a tour. If you plan to see several sights, renting a car or motorbike is more convenient and better value.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Chiang Rai hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary by promotion at any given time, so always compare all three before booking — every review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save several hundred baht a night.
